subject: Res: Hosting requirements & residency prioritization — follow-up and next steps
body_preview: Following up from today — can you confirm whether logs + inference must remain in EU-only? Also proposing next steps: compliance doc, tech deep-dive, and procurement timeline.
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.muller@finserv.de>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@finserv.de
Date: 2027-02-20 09:15 CET
Subject: Re: Intro call — residency / hosting clarifications

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call earlier — helpful discussion. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Security and Legal: 
- We require EU-only residency for both inference processing and logs; no US egress for production PII datasets.
- For a pilot (non-production) we can accept a staged approach in eu-central-1, but production must not allow cross-region fallback that routes tokens outside the EU.
- Preferred model: hosted with dedicated capacity in EU (reserved pools) OR private VPC/on-prem if we need full network isolation and HSM-managed keys.
- Latency target: P95 <= 120ms for typical prompt sizes; peak throughput ~200 rps during batch windows.

Procurement: Legal asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence, an overview of data flows (where inference and logs live), and a sketch of the VPC peering option if we go Private. Can you send a short one-pager and the residency checklist?

Regards,
Anna
Anna Müller | Head of AI Infrastructure
FinServ Bank

---
Attachment: residency-checklist.pdf (application/pdf - stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.muller@finserv.de>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20 11:05 CET
Subject: Re: Intro call — residency / hosting clarifications

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the requirements. Quick notes and next steps from our side: 

Thanks for confirming EU-only for both inference and logs — that helps narrow the hosting modes. To summarize options (we'll tailor based on your procurement appetite):

1) Hosted + Dedicated capacity (recommended if you want fast time-to-prod):
  - Dedicated GPU pools in eu-central-1 or eu-west-1 with customer-level isolation.
  - We can disable cross-region fallback for your tenant so no tokens leave EU.
  - Supports KMS/HSM integrations; we can provide an HSM-backed key option for encryption at rest.
  - Pros: fast onboarding, managed scaling, lower ops overhead.
  - Cons: slightly less network isolation than VPC (but meets most enterprise controls).

2) Private (VPC or on-prem):
  - Private control plane + customer-managed VPC peering or on-prem appliance.
  - Full network isolation and direct HSM/KMS control.
  - Pros: maximal compliance posture; no cross-tenant routing.
  - Cons: longer lead time (4–8 weeks), procurement + infra collaboration required.

Given your latency and throughput targets, both can meet them — Dedicated pools with tuning should comfortably hit P95 <= 120ms for the prompt sizes discussed. For pilot we recommend Hosted + Dedicated in eu-central-1, then evaluate Private for production if Legal insists on physical isolation.

Action items we will deliver by EOD tomorrow:
- Short one-pager summarizing the two hosting models + residency guarantees (attached).
- Residency checklist (attaching the PDF you requested).
- SOC 2 Type II summary and pointer to our compliance pack (link).

Proposed next meeting: Technical Deep Dive with your DevOps + our Platform Engineers — Tue 2027-02-23 10:00 CET. Does that work?

Thanks,
Irene
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-hosting-options-onepager.pdf (application/pdf - stub), residency-checklist.pdf (application/pdf - stub)

Irene / Marcus — forwarding Anna's note + Irene's reply. Quick tech notes from my side: 

- We should explicitly call out that we can toggle routing policies per-tenant (disable fallbacks to other regions). I'll draft the exact config knobs for the tech deep dive.
- For the Dedicated path, we should offer two quantization/latency profiles: low-latency (bigger GPU allocation) vs cost-optimized. FinServ's latency target suggests low-latency profile.
- If Legal needs HSM on customer keys, confirm whether they require an external HSM (customer-managed) or Redwood-managed HSM in EU. For Private on-prem they will have the former.

Proposed internal ask list before the TD: 
  1) Marcus — can you sketch the network diagram options (VPC peering vs private endpoint) we can present?
  2) Marcus/Infra — estimate lead time for Private deployment (we've said 4–8 weeks) and call out any pre-reqs for their side (e.g., subnet size, peering approvals).
  3) Irene — I'll prepare cost delta examples between Dedicated vs Private for a 6-month pilot (tokens + reserved GPU cost).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-21 09:30 CET
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro call — residency / hosting clarifications

Ben / Irene — sketching high-level options below; I'll prepare a diagram before the TD.

Option A — Hosted (Dedicated pool in EU):
- Tenant-level isolation + dedicated GPU nodes.
- No public IP exposure; traffic terminates at our EU ingress endpoints.
- Residency guarantee: disable cross-region routing + keep logs in EU storage buckets.
- Identity: integrate with customer SAML + optional bring-your-own-key via KMS connector (Redwood-managed HSM or customer-managed KMS via peering).

Option B — Private VPC:
- Private control plane (we still manage control plane but data path sits in customer VPC or via Direct Connect).
- Full network ACLs under customer's control.
- HSM: customer can bring HSM; we support both PKCS#11 and cloud HSM connectors.
- Lead time: estimate 6 weeks for configuration + validation (depends on their infra team availability).

Potential gotchas to cover in TD:
- Logging: we need to confirm retention windows and whether logs must land in their S3-equivalent (we can push logs to customer bucket in EU).
- Auditability: provide request-level trace + token-level cost breakdown (for procurement).

I'll attach a quick diagram and the checklist before Tue.

Marcus
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks,
Irene
